steps.detail: 6700 captured rolls fit the uniform lattice and show no serial dependence (informational — the distribution is proven exactly by Step 5's recomputation and the 2M-draw census, Step 16): KS vs Uniform[0,10000] D=0.0138 p=0.1561 (>0.05); lag-1 z=1.873 (|z|<3); runs p=0.0335 (≥0.01)

profileChecks.note: the 6,700 captured rolls are fitted to the uniform lattice (Kolmogorov–Smirnov against the discrete-uniform CDF) and tested for serial dependence (lag-1 autocorrelation and a Wald–Wolfowitz runs test), in capture order. INFORMATIONAL and verdict-light by design — a 6,700-roll sample has little power, so a deviation is reported as INFO (never a FLAG or a hard fail, never counted, verdict unchanged — profile policy INFORMATIONAL, adopted 2026-09-29); the distribution itself is proven EXACTLY by Step 5's per-bet recomputation and the 2M-draw census (Step 16). It is a scored step because its statistics REACT to the sample: the mutation battery corrupts the captured rolls, the step prints [INFO] and the run exits non-zero (M21), so it is falsifiable rather than a vacuous always-PASS (mechanism ported from HouseBets Steps 11 & 13)

packageChecks.artifact: tests/dice/DiceTests.ts (Operator source block) + src/rng.ts OPERATOR_SOURCE_CITES + src/operator-verifier.ts + Step 5
packageChecks.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-25. This note used to say Duel ships no source, so the citation was to the fairness page (E03, which shows the code panel collapsed). Duel publishes the Dice code on its Verify tab; the auditor copied it verbatim on 2026-09-25 (duel.com → Provably Fair → Verify → Expand → Copy) to evidence/verify-tab/duel-verify-tab-dice-2026-09-25.js (E13, SHA-256 38b257c6…), pinned with its runner in src/operator-verifier.ts. The asserts, each met: (1) "unit tests reproduce at least one captured bet from its revealed seed … against the operator's published algorithm" — the Operator source block in tests/dice/DiceTests.ts EXECUTES that file unmodified on all 6,700 captured bets: its validateDiceResult string ((value % 10001) / 100).toString(), mapped onto the 0..10000 lattice by rollUnits (which rejects any string that is not exactly String(units / 100)), equals the served roll and src/rng.ts on 6,700/6,700; (2) "fixed vectors" — the same block requires it to print each of the 7 known rolls exactly as units / 100; (3) "the adapter cites the operator source line it ports" — src/rng.ts OPERATOR_SOURCE_CITES names 12 lines (L28 hex-decoded key … L66 value % RANGE, L74 throw) with the text each must carry, and checkOperatorCites FAILs any that does not: 12/12. Step 5 runs the same execution (plus the file's own RANGE / MAX_FAIR against src/rng.ts) and citation check in the verifier. FAIL probed: M05c (a logic line of the operator file changed AND re-pinned → disagreement), M05d (a byte changed without re-pin → hash mismatch), M05e (a citation moved to a line that does not carry its text). Not established: that the Verify button, or Duel's server, runs exactly this code

npm test = mocha + verify (NO simulate): verify scores the pinned artifacts, re-derives the simulation statistics from the committed census, writes only to outputs/run/ and field-diffs at ATOL 1e-14 / RTOL 1e-12 — the pinned outputs/simulation-results.json is never rewritten by npm test. Regeneration is a separate npm run test:full (simulate writes to outputs/run/, then verify), so a fresh npm ci clone reproduces to Full Pass with the pinned artifacts untouched. Engines pinned to Node 22.x, audit ID PF-2026-DL02 assigned, and a dependency-free standalone verify.js (built from repo root via audit-framework/tools/build-standalone-verifier.mjs) runs the whole verdict under `node verify.js` with zero npm install

M17 forges one epoch's served-band return) and the informational live-fit step (M21 orders the captured rolls so Step 21 flags); added 2026-09-24: the Step 6 empty-seed control (M06b), one-1e-18-unit forgeries of a win credit (M07c) and a multiplier (M09b) that the former tolerances passed, the Step 7 stake-price comparison (M07d) and a byte-only change to a pinned artifact that only the Step 12 pin sees (M12d);
